question.text: How many New World screwworm cases will be confirmed in Mexico in total before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the total number of animal cases of New World screwworm in Mexico before July 1, 2027, according to the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) [Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service current status report](https://www.aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultry-disease/stop-screwworm/current-status?page=1), rounded to the nearest 500.
question.fine_print:
The map and list of cases is updated on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 5:00 p.m. ET by the USDA. This question will resolve as the total number of animal cases on the latest report before July 1, 2027, provided this is published at the earliest by June 1, 2027.

If the USDA ceases reporting or significantly changes its criteria such that previous reporting is not comparable, this question will be **annulled**.

# Research brief: New World screwworm (NWS) animal cases in Mexico before July 2027

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-12: I fetched the APHIS current-status page. Its case map loads with JavaScript, so I could not see the Mexico total. The page was last modified 2026-11-10, says the map updates on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and links to SENASICA's dashboard for Mexico data. [APHIS](https://www.aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultry-disease/stop-screwworm/current-status?page=1)
- APHIS appears to repeat SENASICA's cumulative count, though I have not verified that directly. The question background gives the APHIS figure as 20,591 through 2026-04-15, which sits between SENASICA's ~16,628 (March) and 23,779 (2026-05-08). The forecaster should check the APHIS map by hand.

## 2. Current status
- 2026-11-03: SENASICA's cumulative total was 50,967 cases (counted from 2024-11-20) in 30 states. Only Baja California and Baja California Sur have no cases. This figure came from a search summary and I could not confirm it in a primary document.
- 2026-10-31: The confirmed figure is 50,667 cumulative cases, of which 28,626 were cattle, plus 1,958 active cases (1,019 cattle, 567 dogs). [Zolo Noticias](https://www.zolonoticias.com/2026/11/02/chihuahua-reporta-130-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-al-cierre-de-octubre/)
- 2026-11-10: Active cases nationally were 1,544, down from 1,966 around 2026-11-03 and 2,037 on 2026-10-28. [Periódico Correo Nov 10](https://periodicocorreo.com.mx/vida-publica/2026/nov/10/bajan-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-en-guanajuato-leon-esta-en-primer-lugar-con-14-171246.html), [Nov 3](https://periodicocorreo.com.mx/vida-publica/2026/nov/03/guanajuato-inicia-el-mes-con-repunte-de-casi-90-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-170673.html)
- Nothing has settled the question. The count already exceeds the 30,000 bottom of the question's range. Cumulative totals cannot go down unless cases are revised.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

Weekly pace, in rough terms:
- Dec 2025 to Jan 2026: ~400-500/week
- Jan to Apr 2026: ~520/week
- Apr to Jun 2026: ~1,200-1,500/week
- Jul to Aug 2026: ~1,050/week
- Aug to Oct 2026: ~1,000-1,250/week

Seasonality: there is only one comparable earlier season, since the Mexico series starts in November 2024.
- From mid-November 2025 (about 10,900, estimated backward from the Dec 5 figure) to about 2026-06-30 (about 31,000-33,000), the count rose by roughly 21,000-23,000.
- Growth was slow over winter (Dec to Mar, about 400-550/week) and sped up from April to June.
- The 2026 level is running about 4.6 times the November 2025 level. Weekly additions are now about 2 to 2.5 times last winter's rate.
- For scale only: adding the last winter's ~22,000 to the current ~51,000 gives about 73,000. Repeating the current ~1,100/week for 33 weeks gives about 87,000. These are calculations, not forecasts.
- Active cases are falling now (2,037 to 1,544 in two weeks). That could signal slower new-case confirmations this month.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on Mexico's case count.
- The markets that were already collected are about different questions:

- Experts say pushing the fly back to Panama could take up to a decade. [bdnews24](https://bdnews24.com/health/b2zy8oxune)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Winter (Dec to Feb): last season, case additions slowed sharply. Warm, humid spring weather (April to June 2027) brought the fastest growth.
- Metapa plant ramp-up toward 100M flies/week. One source says full output won't come until November 2027.
- Texas Moore Air Base plant, due mid-2027. It is unlikely to affect Mexico's counts before July.
- Possible US-Mexico cattle import decisions, and Coahuila's export inspection.
- Data cadence: APHIS updates on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The report that resolves the question will be the last one before 2027-07-01, around June 29 or 30.
- I found no official seasonal weather outlook for Mexico through June 2027.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 33 weeks. The resolving report will be the last APHIS update before July 1, 2027, probably June 29 or 30, 2027.

(b) **Latest known value:** About 50,667 cumulative confirmed cases as of 2026-10-31, from the SENASICA series. A search summary put it at about 50,967 on 2026-11-03, but I could not confirm that in a primary document. APHIS appears to track the same series: its 20,591 on April 15 fits SENASICA's numbers either side of that date.

(c) **If nothing changed:** No new cases would leave about 51,000. Cumulative counts cannot fall, so this is a hard floor.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** The recent pace is about 1,000-1,250 per week. Over 34 weeks that adds about 34,000-40,000, giving roughly 85,000-90,000.

However, active cases have dropped from 2,037 to 1,544 in two weeks, which points to fewer new confirmations right now. Last year winter growth slowed to roughly 40% of the spring pace. My estimate:
- November to February, about 17 weeks at about 750-900 per week: roughly 13,000-15,000.
- March to June, about 17 weeks at about 1,000-1,500 per week: roughly 17,000-25,000.

That puts the central estimate near 81,000.

(e) **Historical variation:** Over the comparable period last season, mid-November 2025 to the end of June 2026, the count rose by about 21,000-23,000, from a much smaller base. Weekly pace has ranged from about 400 to 1,500 cases. Over 33 weeks that implies additions anywhere from roughly 15,000 to 50,000.

(f) **Experts and markets:** No market covers this quantity. Experts expect a multi-year fight, with pushing the fly back to Panama possibly taking up to a decade. More sterile flies are coming: the Metapa plant is ramping up, but full output may not arrive until late 2027, and the Texas plant opens mid-2027. These may only modestly slow case growth before July 2027.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** A harsh, dry winter combined with ramped-up sterile-fly releases and stronger animal movement controls could collapse new cases to about 300-500 per week. The total would then end near 62,000-68,000.
- **High:** A warm, wet spring and spread into the northern cattle states could push weekly cases to 2,000 or more by April to June 2027. The total would then exceed 100,000.
